1. Notation and definitions

This paper consists entirely of definitions and observations — no formal proofs appear. The chunker should emit definition and section chunks with zero proof chunks. This exercises the no-proof acceptance criterion for the fixture suite.

Definition 1.1 (Sheaf).

A presheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on a topological space $X$ is a sheaf if it satisfies the gluing and locality axioms for every open cover.

Definition 1.2 (Stalk).

The stalk of a sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ at a point $x \in X$ is the colimit $\mathcal{F}_x = \mathrm{colim}_{U \ni x} \mathcal{F}(U)$ over open neighborhoods of $x$.

Definition 1.3 (Morphism of sheaves).

A morphism $\phi : \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}$ of sheaves is a natural transformation of the underlying presheaves compatible with all restriction maps.

Remark 1.4.

The category of sheaves on $X$ is abelian; this is the starting point of homological algebra in algebraic geometry.

2. Standard examples

A second section with prose that the chunker emits as a section chunk. No proofs appear in this section either.

Example 2.1.

The constant sheaf $\underline{\mathbb{Z}}$ assigns the group $\mathbb{Z}$ to every connected open set.
